```java
        assertThat(dashboard.averageScore()).isEqualByComparingTo("6.50");
        assertThat(dashboard.levelCounts()).containsEntry(SignalLevel.STRONG_BUY, 1);
        assertThat(dashboard.levelCounts()).containsEntry(SignalLevel.SELL, 1);
    }

    @Test
    void excludesATickerWithNoSourcesFromTheAverageAndTheLevelCounts() {
        when(transactionRepository.findAll()).thenReturn(List.of(holding(QQQ), holding(EC)));
        when(snapshotRepository.findLatest(QQQ)).thenReturn(Optional.of(
                snapshot(QQQ, Map.of(SignalSource.TECHNICAL, new BigDecimal("8")))));
        when(snapshotRepository.findLatest(EC)).thenReturn(Optional.of(snapshot(EC, Map.of())));

        SignalsDashboard dashboard = useCase.execute();

        assertThat(dashboard.averageScore()).isEqualByComparingTo("8.00");
        assertThat(dashboard.levelCounts().values()).containsExactly(1);
        assertThat(dashboard.tickersWithoutData()).containsExactly(EC);
        assertThat(dashboard.signals()).hasSize(2);
    }

    @Test
    void treatsATickerWithNoStoredSnapshotAsWithoutData() {
        when(transactionRepository.findAll()).thenReturn(List.of(holding(QQQ)));
        when(snapshotRepository.findLatest(QQQ)).thenReturn(Optional.empty());

        SignalsDashboard dashboard = useCase.execute();

        assertThat(dashboard.tickersWithoutData()).containsExactly(QQQ);
        assertThat(dashboard.averageScore()).isEqualByComparingTo("0.00");
    }

    @Test
    void anEmptyPortfolioProducesAnEmptyDashboard() {
        when(transactionRepository.findAll()).thenReturn(List.of());

        SignalsDashboard dashboard = useCase.execute();

        assertThat(dashboard.signals()).isEmpty();
        assertThat(dashboard.tickersWithoutData()).isEmpty();
        assertThat(dashboard.averageScore()).isEqualByComparingTo("0.00");
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the use cases**

```java
package co.com.david.inversiones.usecase.signal;

import co.com.david.inversiones.model.*;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.SignalSnapshotRepository;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.TransactionRepository;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.RoundingMode;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * Builds the signals dashboard for every instrument currently held.
 *
 * <p>Rows are ordered by combined score descending, highest conviction first. A ticker with no
 * snapshot, or a snapshot with no sources, is listed in
 * {@link SignalsDashboard#tickersWithoutData()} and excluded from the average and the level counts:
 * a zero-source score maps to a strong sell, and including it would fabricate a recommendation
 * nobody made.
 */
public class GetSignalsDashboardUseCase {

    private static final int SCALE = 2;

    private final TransactionRepository transactionRepository;
    private final SignalSnapshotRepository snapshotRepository;

    public GetSignalsDashboardUseCase(TransactionRepository transactionRepository,
                                      SignalSnapshotRepository snapshotRepository) {
        this.transactionRepository = transactionRepository;
        this.snapshotRepository = snapshotRepository;
    }

    public SignalsDashboard execute() {
        Set<Ticker> held = heldTickers();

        List<TickerSignal> signals = new ArrayList<>();
        List<Ticker> withoutData = new ArrayList<>();

        for (Ticker ticker : held) {
            SignalSnapshot snapshot = snapshotRepository.findLatest(ticker)
                    .orElseGet(() -> SignalSnapshot.builder()
                            .ticker(ticker).snapshotDate(LocalDate.EPOCH).scores(Map.of()).build());
            CombinedScore score = CombinedScore.from(snapshot);
            signals.add(new TickerSignal(ticker, snapshot, score));
            if (score.usedSources().isEmpty()) {
                withoutData.add(ticker);
            }
        }

        signals.sort(Comparator.comparing((TickerSignal signal) -> signal.score().value()).reversed());

        List<TickerSignal> scored = signals.stream()
                .filter(signal -> !signal.score().usedSources().isEmpty())
                .toList();

        return SignalsDashboard.builder()
                .signals(signals)
                .averageScore(averageOf(scored))
                .levelCounts(countLevels(scored))
                .tickersWithoutData(withoutData)
                .build();
    }

    private Set<Ticker> heldTickers() {
        return Position.deriveAll(transactionRepository.findAll()).stream()
                .map(Position::ticker)
                .collect(Collectors.toCollection(LinkedHashSet::new));
    }

    private BigDecimal averageOf(List<TickerSignal> scored) {
        if (scored.isEmpty()) {
            return BigDecimal.ZERO.setScale(SCALE, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
        }
        BigDecimal total = scored.stream()
                .map(signal -> signal.score().value())
                .reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add);
        return total.divide(new BigDecimal(scored.size()), SCALE, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
    }

    private Map<SignalLevel, Integer> countLevels(List<TickerSignal> scored) {
        Map<SignalLevel, Integer> counts = new EnumMap<>(SignalLevel.class);
        for (TickerSignal signal : scored) {
            counts.merge(signal.score().level(), 1, Integer::sum);
        }
        return counts;
    }
}
```

```java
package co.com.david.inversiones.usecase.signal;

import co.com.david.inversiones.model.Position;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.SignalSnapshot;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.Ticker;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.SignalProvider;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.SignalSnapshotRepository;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.TimeProvider;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.TransactionRepository;

import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * Pulls today's signals for every held instrument and stores them as a historical snapshot.
 *
 * <p>Intended to run on a schedule after the upstream workflows have refreshed their own caches. A
 * provider that returns nothing stores nothing and reports zero, leaving the previous day's
 * snapshots intact rather than erasing history over a transient upstream failure.
 */
public class RefreshSignalSnapshotUseCase {

    private final TransactionRepository transactionRepository;
    private final SignalProvider signalProvider;
    private final SignalSnapshotRepository snapshotRepository;
    private final TimeProvider timeProvider;

    public RefreshSignalSnapshotUseCase(TransactionRepository transactionRepository,
                                        SignalProvider signalProvider,
                                        SignalSnapshotRepository snapshotRepository,
                                        TimeProvider timeProvider) {
        this.transactionRepository = transactionRepository;
        this.signalProvider = signalProvider;
        this.snapshotRepository = snapshotRepository;
        this.timeProvider = timeProvider;
    }

    /** @return how many snapshots were stored */
    public int execute() {
        Set<Ticker> held = Position.deriveAll(transactionRepository.findAll()).stream()
                .map(Position::ticker)
                .collect(Collectors.toCollection(LinkedHashSet::new));

        if (held.isEmpty()) {
            return 0;
        }

        List<SignalSnapshot> fetched = signalProvider.fetchSnapshots(held, timeProvider.today());
        if (fetched.isEmpty()) {
            return 0;
        }

        return snapshotRepository.saveAll(fetched).size();
    }
}
```

### Task 11: Diversification rules

**Files:**
- Create: `model/DiversificationLimit.java`, `model/DiversificationViolation.java`, `model/DiversificationReport.java`
- Create: `usecase/portfolio/EvaluateDiversificationUseCase.java`
- Test: `usecase/portfolio/EvaluateDiversificationUseCaseTest.java`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `PortfolioValuation`, `ValuedPosition`, `Instrument`, `InstrumentType`, `InstrumentRepository`, `Percentage`, `GetPortfolioUseCase` (Tasks 3–7).
- Produces:
  - `DiversificationLimit` enum `SINGLE_EQUITY` (20), `SINGLE_ETF` (25), `SECTOR` (30), each with `Percentage allowedWeight()`.
  - `DiversificationViolation` record `(DiversificationLimit limit, String subject, Percentage actualWeight, Percentage allowedWeight)`.
  - `DiversificationReport` — builder over `List<DiversificationViolation> violations`, `Money totalMarketValue`, `Map<String, Percentage> weightByTicker`, `Map<String, Percentage> weightBySector`, plus `boolean compliant()` returning `violations().isEmpty()`.
  - `EvaluateDiversificationUseCase(GetPortfolioUseCase, InstrumentRepository)` with `execute() -> DiversificationReport`.

**The rules being encoded.** From the investor profile: at most 20% of the portfolio in any single stock, at most 25% in any single ETF, at most 30% in any one sector. Weights are computed on **market value**, not cost, because that is the exposure actually carried today. Holdings of the same ticker at different brokers are **added together** for the ticker limit — they are one exposure regardless of where they sit, and evaluating them separately would let two 15% lots hide a 30% concentration. An instrument missing from the catalog is treated as an equity in an `UNKNOWN` sector, so it counts toward the stricter limit rather than escaping the check.

```java
package co.com.david.inversiones.model;

/** The allocation ceilings of the investor profile, as a share of total market value. */
public enum DiversificationLimit {

    /** At most 20% of the portfolio in any single stock. */
    SINGLE_EQUITY(Percentage.of("20")),
    /** At most 25% of the portfolio in any single fund. */
    SINGLE_ETF(Percentage.of("25")),
    /** At most 30% of the portfolio in any one sector. */
    SECTOR(Percentage.of("30"));

    private final Percentage allowedWeight;

    DiversificationLimit(Percentage allowedWeight) {
        this.allowedWeight = allowedWeight;
    }

    public Percentage allowedWeight() {
        return allowedWeight;
    }
}
```

```java
/**
 * One breached allocation ceiling.
 *
 * @param subject the ticker or sector name that is over its limit
 */
public record DiversificationViolation(DiversificationLimit limit, String subject,
                                       Percentage actualWeight, Percentage allowedWeight) {
}
```

```java
package co.com.david.inversiones.usecase.portfolio;

import co.com.david.inversiones.model.*;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.InstrumentRepository;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Checks the portfolio against the allocation ceilings of the investor profile.
 *
 * <p>Weights are computed on market value, which is the exposure actually carried today rather than
 * the one that was bought. Lots of the same ticker held at different brokers are added together:
 * they are one exposure, and checking them separately would let two 15% lots hide a 30%
 * concentration. An instrument absent from the catalog is treated as an equity in an unknown sector
 * so that it falls under the stricter ceiling instead of escaping the check.
 */
public class EvaluateDiversificationUseCase {

    private static final String UNKNOWN_SECTOR = "UNKNOWN";

    private final GetPortfolioUseCase getPortfolio;
    private final InstrumentRepository instrumentRepository;

    public EvaluateDiversificationUseCase(GetPortfolioUseCase getPortfolio,
                                          InstrumentRepository instrumentRepository) {
        this.getPortfolio = getPortfolio;
        this.instrumentRepository = instrumentRepository;
    }

    public DiversificationReport execute() {
        PortfolioValuation valuation = getPortfolio.execute();
        Money total = valuation.totalMarketValue();

        Map<String, Money> valueByTicker = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        Map<String, Money> valueBySector = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        Map<String, InstrumentType> typeByTicker = new LinkedHashMap<>();

        for (ValuedPosition position : valuation.positions()) {
            Ticker ticker = position.position().ticker();
            Optional<Instrument> instrument = instrumentRepository.findByTicker(ticker);
            InstrumentType type = instrument.map(Instrument::type).orElse(InstrumentType.EQUITY);
            String sector = instrument.map(Instrument::sector).orElse(UNKNOWN_SECTOR);

            typeByTicker.put(ticker.symbol(), type);
            valueByTicker.merge(ticker.symbol(), position.marketValue(), Money::add);
            valueBySector.merge(sector, position.marketValue(), Money::add);
        }

        Map<String, Percentage> weightByTicker = weights(valueByTicker, total);
        Map<String, Percentage> weightBySector = weights(valueBySector, total);

        List<DiversificationViolation> violations = new ArrayList<>();
        weightByTicker.forEach((symbol, weight) -> {
            DiversificationLimit limit = typeByTicker.get(symbol).isFund()
                    ? DiversificationLimit.SINGLE_ETF
                    : DiversificationLimit.SINGLE_EQUITY;
            addIfBreached(violations, limit, symbol, weight);
        });
        weightBySector.forEach((sector, weight) ->
                addIfBreached(violations, DiversificationLimit.SECTOR, sector, weight));

        return DiversificationReport.builder()
                .violations(violations)
                .totalMarketValue(total)
                .weightByTicker(weightByTicker)
                .weightBySector(weightBySector)
                .build();
    }

    private Map<String, Percentage> weights(Map<String, Money> values, Money total) {
        Map<String, Percentage> weights = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        values.forEach((key, value) -> weights.put(key, Percentage.between(value, total)));
        return weights;
    }

    private void addIfBreached(List<DiversificationViolation> violations, DiversificationLimit limit,
                               String subject, Percentage actual) {
        if (actual.value().compareTo(limit.allowedWeight().value()) > 0) {
            violations.add(new DiversificationViolation(limit, subject, actual, limit.allowedWeight()));
        }
    }
}
```

### Task 12: Authentication use case and the coverage gate

**Files:**
- Create: `model/User.java`, `model/AuthenticatedSession.java`, `model/exception/InvalidCredentialsException.java`
- Create: `model/gateways/UserRepository.java`, `model/gateways/PasswordHasher.java`, `model/gateways/TokenProvider.java`
- Create: `usecase/auth/AuthenticateUserUseCase.java`
- Modify: `backend/main.gradle` (JaCoCo verification rule)
- Test: `usecase/auth/AuthenticateUserUseCaseTest.java`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `TimeProvider` (Task 6).
- Produces:
  - `User` — builder over `Long id`, `String username`, `String passwordHash`.
  - `AuthenticatedSession` record `(String token, Instant expiresAt, String username)`.
  - `UserRepository`: `Optional<User> findByUsername(String username)`.
  - `PasswordHasher`: `String hash(String rawPassword)`, `boolean matches(String rawPassword, String passwordHash)`.
  - `TokenProvider`: `AuthenticatedSession issue(User user)`.
  - `AuthenticateUserUseCase(UserRepository, PasswordHasher, TokenProvider)` with `execute(String username, String rawPassword) -> AuthenticatedSession`.

**The rule being encoded.** An unknown username and a wrong password produce the **same** exception with the same message. Distinguishing them tells an attacker which usernames exist. The password is verified through the `PasswordHasher` port so the domain never learns which algorithm is used.

```java
package co.com.david.inversiones.usecase.auth;

import co.com.david.inversiones.model.AuthenticatedSession;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.User;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.exception.InvalidCredentialsException;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.PasswordHasher;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.TokenProvider;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.UserRepository;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.InjectMocks;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;

import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.Optional;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;
import static org.mockito.ArgumentMatchers.any;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.*;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class AuthenticateUserUseCaseTest {

    private static final String USERNAME = "david";
    private static final String PASSWORD = "correct-horse";
    private static final String HASH = "$2a$10$storedhash";

    @Mock
    private UserRepository userRepository;
    @Mock
    private PasswordHasher passwordHasher;
    @Mock
    private TokenProvider tokenProvider;
    @InjectMocks
    private AuthenticateUserUseCase useCase;

    private static User user() {
        return User.builder().id(1L).username(USERNAME).passwordHash(HASH).build();
    }

    @Test
    void issuesASessionForValidCredentials() {
        AuthenticatedSession session =
                new AuthenticatedSession("jwt-token", Instant.parse("2026-09-30T00:00:00Z"), USERNAME);
        when(userRepository.findByUsername(USERNAME)).thenReturn(Optional.of(user()));
        when(passwordHasher.matches(PASSWORD, HASH)).thenReturn(true);
        when(tokenProvider.issue(any(User.class))).thenReturn(session);

        assertThat(useCase.execute(USERNAME, PASSWORD)).isSameAs(session);
    }

    @Test
    void rejectsAWrongPassword() {
        when(userRepository.findByUsername(USERNAME)).thenReturn(Optional.of(user()));
        when(passwordHasher.matches("wrong", HASH)).thenReturn(false);

        assertThatThrownBy(() -> useCase.execute(USERNAME, "wrong"))
                .isInstanceOf(InvalidCredentialsException.class);
        verify(tokenProvider, never()).issue(any());
    }

    @Test
    void rejectsAnUnknownUsernameWithTheSameMessageAsAWrongPassword() {
        when(userRepository.findByUsername("ghost")).thenReturn(Optional.empty());
        when(userRepository.findByUsername(USERNAME)).thenReturn(Optional.of(user()));
        when(passwordHasher.matches("wrong", HASH)).thenReturn(false);

        String unknownUser = catchMessage(() -> useCase.execute("ghost", PASSWORD));
        String wrongPassword = catchMessage(() -> useCase.execute(USERNAME, "wrong"));

        assertThat(unknownUser).isEqualTo(wrongPassword);
    }

    @Test
    void doesNotConsultTheHasherWhenTheUserDoesNotExist() {
        when(userRepository.findByUsername("ghost")).thenReturn(Optional.empty());

        assertThatThrownBy(() -> useCase.execute("ghost", PASSWORD))
                .isInstanceOf(InvalidCredentialsException.class);
        verifyNoInteractions(passwordHasher, tokenProvider);
    }

    private static String catchMessage(Runnable action) {
        try {
            action.run();
            throw new AssertionError("Expected InvalidCredentialsException");
        } catch (InvalidCredentialsException exception) {
            return exception.getMessage();
        }
    }
}
```

`User` — hand-written builder following `Transaction.Builder` over `Long id`, `String username`, `String passwordHash`, with `username` and `passwordHash` required. Its `toString()` must **not** include `passwordHash`; override it to return only the id and username so a stray log line cannot leak the hash.

Write the three ports in `model/gateways/` exactly as given in the Interfaces block. `PasswordHasher` documents that `matches` must be a constant-time comparison, which is the implementation's obligation, not the domain's.

```java
package co.com.david.inversiones.usecase.auth;

import co.com.david.inversiones.model.AuthenticatedSession;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.User;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.exception.InvalidCredentialsException;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.PasswordHasher;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.TokenProvider;
import co.com.david.inversiones.model.gateways.UserRepository;

/**
 * Verifies credentials and issues a session.
 *
 * <p>An unknown username and a wrong password fail identically, with the same exception and the same
 * message: telling them apart would let a caller enumerate which usernames exist.
 */
public class AuthenticateUserUseCase {

    private final UserRepository userRepository;
    private final PasswordHasher passwordHasher;
    private final TokenProvider tokenProvider;

    public AuthenticateUserUseCase(UserRepository userRepository,
                                   PasswordHasher passwordHasher,
                                   TokenProvider tokenProvider) {
        this.userRepository = userRepository;
        this.passwordHasher = passwordHasher;
        this.tokenProvider = tokenProvider;
    }

    public AuthenticatedSession execute(String username, String rawPassword) {
        User user = userRepository.findByUsername(username)
                .orElseThrow(InvalidCredentialsException::new);

        if (!passwordHasher.matches(rawPassword, user.passwordHash())) {
            throw new InvalidCredentialsException();
        }

        return tokenProvider.issue(user);
    }
}
```

In `backend/main.gradle`, inside the existing `subprojects { ... }` block, add a JaCoCo verification rule and make `check` depend on it:

```groovy
    jacocoTestCoverageVerification {
        violationRules {
            rule {
                limit {
                    counter = 'LINE'
                    minimum = 0.80
                }
            }
        }
        afterEvaluate {
            classDirectories.setFrom(files(classDirectories.files.collect {
                fileTree(dir: it, exclude: [
                        '**/config/**',
                        '**/MainApplication*',
                        '**/*Application*'
                ])
            }))
        }
    }

    check.dependsOn jacocoTestCoverageVerification
```

## Out of Scope (later plans)

Plan 2 implements the ports: `jpa-repository` with Flyway and Testcontainers, `rest-consumer` against n8n with Resilience4j, `security-jwt`, the REST entry point with OpenAPI, and Cucumber acceptance tests. `AiSynthesisProvider`, `EarningsProvider`, `WatchlistProvider` and `FundamentalsProvider` are declared there together with the use cases that read them, since they carry no business rule beyond passing data through. Plan 3 is the frontend, Plan 4 is Docker, Jenkins and deployment.
